label: Class 2
name: Class 2
blurb: Hundreds, equal groups, lines and data.

chapters.title: Hundreds, tens and ones
chapters.tagline: Build, compare and say three-digit numbers like 342.
outcomes: I can read hundreds, tens and ones.
I can order and compare numbers.
I can match a three-digit number to its written name.

vocab.meaning: Ten tens. A big group of 100.
One of the symbols 0 to 9. Where a digit sits gives its value.
The job a digit does: hundreds, tens or ones.

see.title: Ten tens make one hundred
text: Ten ones make a ten. Ten tens make a hundred.
Here is one hundred: 10 rows with 10 dots in each row.

c.caption: One hundred is ten tens: 10 rows of 10.

see.title: Read a three-digit number
text: The number 342 has three digits.
3 is hundreds, 4 is tens and 2 is ones. So 342 is 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 2 ones.

c.caption: 342 is 300 and 42. The 42 is 4 tens and 2 ones.

see.title: A zero holds the place
text: In 305 there are 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones.
The zero says there are no tens. It keeps the 5 in the ones place.

c.caption: 305 is 300 and 5. There are no tens.

see.title: Which number is bigger?
text: Compare the hundreds first. If they match, compare the tens, then the ones.
342 and 324 have 3 hundreds. 4 tens is more than 2 tens, so 342 is bigger.

c.caption: 342 is further along the line than 324.

see.title: Say the number name
text: Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.
342 is said "three hundred and forty-two".

c.caption: 300 + 40 + 2 = three hundred and forty-two.

try.prompt: This shows 3 tens and 14 ones. Swap 10 ones for 1 ten, then look at what is left.
try.success: 3 tens and 14 ones is the same as 4 tens and 4 ones: 44.
try.hint: Press the swap button once. Then count the tens and ones.

try.prompt: Move the marker to 347 on the number line.
try.hint: Start at 340 and count 7 steps to the right.

try.prompt: Make a hundred. Add tens one at a time until 10 tens trade for 1 hundred.
try.success: Ten tens make 1 hundred, so the number is 100.
try.hint: Press + under Tens ten times. Watch the Hundreds column.

chapters.title: Add, subtract and make equal groups
chapters.tagline: Add and take away with swaps, count equal groups and find the missing part.
outcomes: I can add and subtract in a story.
I can count equal groups.
I can find a missing digit or amount.

vocab.meaning: Trade 10 ones for 1 ten, or 1 ten for 10 ones. The amount stays the same.
Groups with the same number of things in each.
Things in neat rows and columns, so equal groups are easy to count.

see.title: Add with a swap
text: 38 + 27: add the ones first. 8 + 7 = 15 ones.
15 ones is too many. Swap 10 ones for 1 ten. Then 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 tens, so the answer is 65.

c.caption: 3 tens + 2 tens = 5 tens. 8 + 7 = 15 ones. Swap 10 ones for 1 ten: 65.

see.title: Take away with a swap
text: 52 − 27: you cannot take 7 ones from 2 ones.
Swap 1 ten for 10 ones. Now 52 is 4 tens and 12 ones. Take away 2 tens and 7 ones: 25 left.

c.caption: 52 is 4 tens and 12 ones. Take away 2 tens and 7 ones. 25 are left.

see.title: Equal groups
text: 3 plates with 4 biscuits on each plate.
Count in 4s: 4, 8, 12. So 3 groups of 4 make 12.

see.title: Jump on a number line
text: Each jump is one group of 4.
Three jumps of 4 start at 0 and land on 12.

c.caption: 3 jumps of 4 land on 12.

see.title: Find the missing part
text: The whole is 73. One part is 45. The other part is hiding.
Take away to find it: 73 − 45 = 28.

c.caption: Whole 73. One part 45. The missing part is 28.

try.prompt: Show 38 + 27. It starts as 5 tens and 15 ones. Swap until the ones are fewer than 10.
try.hint: Swap 10 ones for 1 ten.

try.prompt: Make 4 groups with 5 in each group.
try.hint: Add groups until there are 4. Keep 5 in each group.

try.prompt: The whole is 15 and one part is 9. Add to the second part until the parts make 15.
try.success: 9 and 6 make 15. The missing part is 6.
try.hint: How many more than 9 make 15?

try.prompt: The left side has 12. Add to it until the balance matches the 20 on the right.
try.hint: What must you add to 12 to reach 20?

chapters.title: Find number and picture rules
chapters.tagline: Spot the rule in number rows and growing pictures, then use it again.
outcomes: I can continue a number series.
I can continue a growing picture.
I can use the same rule for a new number.

vocab.meaning: What happens each time, like add 5 or add 2 more tiles.
Numbers in a row that follow a rule.
The small piece that comes round again and again.

see.title: A number series has a rule
text: Look at 5, 10, 15, 20. Each number is 5 more than the one before.
The rule is add 5. The next number is 25.

c.caption: Add 5 each time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25.

see.title: Pictures can repeat
text: Triangle, square, square, triangle, square, square.
The repeat unit is triangle, square, square. It comes round again and again.

c.caption: The repeat unit is triangle, square, square.

see.title: Growing pictures
text: Picture 1 has 1 tile. Picture 2 has 3 tiles. Picture 3 has 5 tiles.
Each picture adds 2 more tiles. Picture 4 will have 7.

c.title: Tiles in each picture
c.caption: Add 2 tiles each time.

see.title: A rule machine
text: A machine follows one rule every time. This machine adds 3.
2 goes in and 5 comes out. 10 goes in and 13 comes out.

c.caption: Add 3: 10 goes in, 13 comes out.

try.prompt: Fill the two missing shapes. Pick a shape, then tap a gap.
try.hint: Find the repeat unit first. It is triangle, square, square.

try.prompt: Count in 5s from 0. Use the hop button until you land on 15.
try.hint: Press Hop forward 5 three times.

try.prompt: Picture 4 follows the rule: 1, 3, 5, then 7. Add tiles to Picture 4.
try.hint: The rule is add 2. What is 5 + 2?

chapters.title: Lines, shapes and solids
chapters.tagline: Count lines and shapes carefully, describe solids and finish a mirror picture.
outcomes: I can count lines and shapes.
I can describe a solid.
I can complete a reflected picture.

vocab.meaning: A straight edge of a flat shape.
The point where two sides meet.
A shape you can hold, like a ball or a box.
A line down the middle. Both halves match.

see.title: Sides and corners
text: A rectangle has 4 straight sides and 4 corners.
Touch each side once as you count. That way you never count one twice.

c.caption: A rectangle: 4 sides and 4 corners.

see.title: Shapes inside shapes
text: Look carefully. A small shape can sit inside a bigger one.
This big square is made of 4 small squares. Count them all: 4 small and 1 big is 5 squares.

c.caption: 4 small squares and 1 big square make 5 squares.

see.title: Solids you can hold
text: A cube has 6 flat faces. A cuboid is a box shape. A cylinder is like a tin.
A cone has a pointed tip. A sphere is round like a ball.

c.caption: Five solids: cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere.

see.title: Roll or slide?
text: A sphere rolls in every direction because it is curved all over.
A cube has flat faces, so it slides and stacks well.

c.caption: Curved solids roll. Flat faces slide and stack.

see.title: Make a mirror picture
text: Fold along the mirror line. The two halves fit exactly.
Every shaded square on one side has a twin on the other side.

c.caption: Both halves match across the mirror line.

try.prompt: Which solids have a pointed tip? Sort all five.
try.success: Only the cone has a pointed tip.
try.hint: Think of an ice-cream cone.

try.prompt: Shade the squares on the right so both halves make a mirror picture.
try.success: Each square has a twin across the mirror line.
try.hint: Tap the square on the right that matches each shaded square on the left.

chapters.title: Length, weight, capacity and temperature
chapters.tagline: Measure from zero, compare weight and capacity, and read a thermometer.
outcomes: I can measure and compare lengths.
I can compare weight and capacity.
I can compare thermometer readings.

vocab.meaning: How long something is, measured in cm or m.
How heavy something is, measured in g or kg.
How much a container holds, measured in mL or litres.
How hot or cold something is, in degrees.

see.title: Start measuring at zero
text: Line up the start of the pencil with 0 on the ruler.
Read the number at the other end. This pencil is 7 cm long.

c.caption: The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 7 cm.

see.title: Heavier and lighter
text: A balance tips down on the heavier side.
Here the right side is heavier. If both sides match, they weigh the same.

see.title: How much fits?
text: Capacity tells how much a jug holds.
Jug B holds 5 cups. Jug A holds 3 cups. Jug B holds 2 cups more.

see.title: Read a thermometer
text: A thermometer scale works like a number line.
Higher up means hotter. 30 degrees is warmer than 25 degrees.

c.caption: The reading is 30 degrees.

try.prompt: A leaf is 8 cm long. Move the marker to the end of the leaf.
try.success: The leaf is 8 cm: the end sits on 8.
try.hint: Start at 0 and count 8 along.

try.prompt: The left side has 6 cubes. The right side has 10. Add cubes to the left until the balance is level.
try.hint: How many more than 6 make 10?

try.prompt: Jug C holds 2 cups more than Jug B. Set Jug C.
try.hint: Jug B holds 4. Add 2.

chapters.title: Clocks, dates and how long
chapters.tagline: Read clocks to the quarter hour, work out how long, and use a calendar.
outcomes: I can match a clock to a time.
I can work out how long something takes.
I can use a calendar or timetable.

vocab.meaning: The minute hand points to 3. It is 15 minutes after the hour.
The minute hand points to 9. It is 15 minutes before the next hour.
How much time passes from a start to an end.

see.title: Read the hour hand first
text: The short hand tells the hour. The long hand tells the minutes.
At 4 o'clock the long hand points to 12 and the short hand points to 4.

see.title: Quarter past
text: A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes.
When the long hand points to 3 it is quarter past. Here it is quarter past 7.

c.caption: Quarter past 7: the long hand points to 3.

see.title: Quarter to
text: When the long hand points to 9, there are 15 minutes to go until the next hour.
Here it is quarter to 9. The short hand is almost on 9.

c.caption: Quarter to 9: the long hand points to 9.

see.title: How long does it take?
text: Count the hours between the start and the end.
School starts at 9 and lunch is at 12. That is 3 hours.

c.caption: From 9 to 12 is 3 hours.

see.title: Use a calendar
text: A week has 7 days. The days sit in the same column every week.
If March 8 is a Sunday, then March 15 is a Sunday too.

try.prompt: Show quarter past 3. Drag the hands or use the buttons.
try.success: Quarter past 3: the long hand is on 3.
try.hint: Put the short hand on 3 and the long hand on 3.

try.prompt: Show quarter to 6. The short hand is just before 6.
try.success: Quarter to 6 is 5:45. The long hand is on 9.
try.hint: Put the long hand on 9 and the short hand near 6.

try.prompt: The picnic is 10 days after March 3. Tap the date.
try.hint: Count on 10 from the 3rd.

chapters.title: Shop, save and find change
chapters.tagline: Make amounts with notes and coins, find change and keep track of savings.
outcomes: I can make an amount with notes and coins.
I can find a missing price or change.
I can compare purchases within a budget.

vocab.meaning: The money you get back when you pay more than the price.
How much something costs.
Money you keep for later instead of spending.

see.title: Coins and notes
text: Rs 1, Rs 2, Rs 5 and Rs 10 can be coins. Rs 10, Rs 20 and Rs 50 can be notes.
Count the biggest first, then add the smaller ones.

c.caption: Rs 50 + Rs 20 + Rs 10 + Rs 5 = Rs 85

see.title: Make an amount
text: To make Rs 27, start with a Rs 20 note.
Add a Rs 5 coin and a Rs 2 coin. 20 + 5 + 2 = 27.

see.title: Find the change
text: A toy costs Rs 35. You pay with a Rs 50 note.
Change is what is left: 50 − 35 = 15.

c.caption: Rs 50 paid. The toy costs Rs 35. The change is Rs 15.

see.title: Spend and save
text: You have Rs 50 saved. You spend Rs 18.
Take away: 50 − 18 = 32. You still have Rs 32.

c.caption: Rs 50 take away Rs 18 leaves Rs 32.

try.prompt: Make Rs 37 with exactly 4 notes and coins.
try.hint: Start with a Rs 20 note. 17 is left to make.

try.prompt: A toy costs Rs 35 and you pay with Rs 50. Put the change in the purse.
try.hint: 50 − 35 is the change.

chapters.title: Read picture charts
chapters.tagline: Read picture graphs, compare the groups and check statements about data.
outcomes: I can use a pictograph key.
I can compare chart values.
I can check a statement about data.

vocab.meaning: A graph that uses pictures to show how many.
Tells you how many each picture stands for.
Marks counted in groups of 5.

see.title: Read the key first
text: A picture graph uses pictures to count. Read the key before you count.
Here every picture means 1 fruit. Apples have 4 pictures, so 4 apples were eaten.

see.title: Compare two bars
text: Dogs have 6 and cats have 4.
Find how many more: 6 − 4 = 2. There are 2 more dogs than cats.

see.title: Tally marks
text: Tally marks go in groups of 5, so they are quick to count.
Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. Three full groups make 15.

c.caption: Three groups of 5 tally marks: 15.

see.title: Is the statement true?
text: Check a statement against the graph. "Mango is eaten more than banana" is true.
Mango has 3 and banana has 2. 3 is more than 2.

try.prompt: Make the picture graph match the table: Cat 3, Dog 5, Fish 2.
try.success: The graph shows Cat 3, Dog 5 and Fish 2.
try.hint: Add one picture for each count in the table.

try.prompt: Red has 3 more than Blue. Blue is 4. Set the Red bar.
try.hint: Add 3 to the Blue count.

try.prompt: Make 4 groups of 5 tally marks.
try.hint: Add groups until there are 4.

chapters.title: Codes, hidden shapes and order
chapters.tagline: Find the odd one out, read simple codes, spot hidden shapes and find places in a row.
outcomes: I can group pictures and use an analogy.
I can use a code key to read a message.
I can find an exact shape hidden in a picture.
I can find a place in a row.

vocab.meaning: The one that does not belong with the others.
A secret way of writing. A key says what each symbol means.
Words for position in a row: first, second, third.

see.title: Odd one out
text: Look for what most pictures share. Then find the one that is different.
The cube and the cuboid have flat faces. The sphere is round, so it is the odd one out.

c.caption: Cube, cuboid and sphere: which is the odd one out?

see.title: Use the same rule
text: Small circle goes with big circle. So small square goes with big square.
The rule is: the second picture is bigger.

c.caption: Small to big, again and again.

see.title: Read a code
text: A code key says what each symbol means. A is 1, B is 2 and C is 3.
So C A B in code is 3 1 2.

c.caption: Code key: C A B is 3 1 2.

see.title: Find a hidden shape
text: A small shape can hide inside a bigger picture.
Find the exact shape, with the same size and turn. Here an L-shape hides in the corner.

c.caption: An L-shape: 3 squares down and 3 squares across.

see.title: Find a place in a row
text: There are 8 children in a row. Mia is 3rd from the left.
Counting from the right, Mia is 6th. The place depends on which end you start from.

c.caption: Mia is 3rd from the left.

try.prompt: Small circle goes with big circle. Fill the gap with the matching big shape.
try.success: The second shape is bigger: small square goes to big square.
try.hint: Look at what changes from the small circle to the big circle.

try.prompt: Code key: A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, D = 4. Put each letter in the box with its code number.
try.success: Each letter matches its number in the key.
try.hint: A comes first, so A is 1.

try.prompt: Sam is 2nd from the right in a row of 8. Move the marker to Sam's place counted from the left.
try.success: 2nd from the right in a row of 8 is 7th from the left.
try.hint: The last place is 8. One in from the last is 7.

parents.idea: Reasoning is thinking clearly about clues. Your child sorts, matches a rule to a new picture, reads a simple code and says who is 1st, 2nd or 3rd in a row.
parents.slip: Children often count from the wrong end of a row. Ask: "Which end are we counting from?" Also check that a hidden shape is the same size, not just similar.

tryAtHome.title: Odd one out at home
steps: Put three spoons and one fork on the table.
Ask which one is the odd one out and why.
Now line up 5 toys. Ask who is 2nd from the left and who is 2nd from the right.
